done_when: A git-ignored forge.local.toml beside forge.toml, read from the main checkout so every task and fix worktree of that clone uses it, overrides only which tools run work, the worker split and the model and effort per kind of work; Forge refuses any other key in it; new and upgraded repos ignore the file in git; forge next and forge doctor show which file each of those settings came from

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `setting_sources` attributes `models.build` to a file whenever that file has a build table, without checking whether it has an entry for the selected worker. In an upgraded repo with only `[models.build.codex]`, setting local `tools = "claude"` makes `forge work` use Claude's built-in default (repo.py:513–530), while `forge next` claims the model came from `forge.toml`. The same check can claim a local model when the local table contains only the other worker's entry. The required per-setting source display is therefore incorrect in a normal worker-switching case.
findings.title: Not done: model sources are misidentified after a local tool switch

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The new source display is added only to ready-task lines. After `forge task start` or `forge fix start`, `forge next` reports the active item through `_item` (nextstep.py:614 onward), which prints the next `forge work` command without any setting sources. A developer checking which local choices will run that work sees no file attribution, although the Done-when requires `forge next` to show it.
findings.title: Not done: forge next omits setting sources for active tasks and fixes

why: Developers on one team have different agent access, but who builds and which models live in the committed forge.toml, so one developer's switch to Codex lands in pull requests and flips teammates' settings
